base_instruction: You are a helpful event catering assistant. Help the user plan food for a memorial service reception by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistical details. When the user asks you to review specific menu items, check each item against every attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to people's dietary situations throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hi, we're organizing a reception after my grandmother's memorial service this Saturday and I need help figuring out the food situation.

flow_info.value: Main family group attending: me, Uncle Richard, Cousin Priya, and Aunt Helen
Uncle Richard had heart surgery two months ago and his doctor put him on a strict low-sodium diet while he recovers
Aunt Helen ate something with peanuts at a party last year and had a severe allergic reaction, had to be rushed to the hospital
Budget is around 25 dollars per person, keeping it simple and respectful
The church hall has a small kitchen we can use to keep things warm
Uncle Richard just came back from his follow-up appointment and his doctor said his recovery is going great, bloodwork is perfect, he can go back to eating normally now
My nephew Marcus is flying in from Denver, he'll make it after all, so add one more person

Aunt Helen's daughter just called me to clarify — it wasn't just peanuts, Helen actually reacted to a mixed nut brownie, and the allergist confirmed she's allergic to all tree nuts too, not just peanuts
Menu items to check: honey-glazed ham, walnut-crusted chicken, Caesar salad with croutons, gluten-free salted caramel brownies, roasted potato wedges, fresh fruit platter

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables including onion, garlic, and potato
constraints.surface_form: Cousin Priya married into the family a few years back, she grew up in a traditional Jain household in Gujarat
inference_chain: Traditional Jain household → practices Jain dietary laws
Jain diet → strict vegetarian, no meat, no fish, no eggs
Jain diet → no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potato, carrots etc.)

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Helen ate something with peanuts at a party last year and had a severe allergic reaction, had to be rushed to the hospital

constraints.value: Cannot eat any tree nuts (walnuts, almonds, cashews, pecans, etc.) in addition to peanuts
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Helen's daughter just called me to clarify — it wasn't just peanuts, Helen actually reacted to a mixed nut brownie, and the allergist confirmed she's allergic to all tree nuts too, not just peanuts

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten or gluten-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago so he has to avoid gluten completely

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a reception after your grandmother's memorial service. You will introduce family members and their dietary needs, receive updates as plans change (Uncle Richard gets medically cleared, nephew Marcus joins, Aunt Helen's allergy scope is corrected), and finally ask the assistant to review a specific menu. You are calm and matter-of-fact about the changes. When presenting the menu at the end, just ask if there are any issues — do not hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, matter-of-fact family organizer dealing with a somber but practical task. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Uncle Richard told me...', 'Priya mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change. You treat each update as normal family coordination. Your tone is warm but understated, appropriate for memorial planning.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family member updates

aims.description: I found a caterer nearby with good reviews. Their reception package includes: honey-glazed ham, walnut-crusted chicken, Caesar salad with croutons, gluten-free salted caramel brownies, roasted potato wedges, and a fresh fruit platter. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 items against all current dietary constraints and identifies specific problems
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Four items have problems. Honey-glazed ham: meat, so Priya cannot eat it (Jain vegetarian). Walnut-crusted chicken: contains walnuts, so Aunt Helen cannot eat it (tree nut allergy); also meat, so Priya cannot eat it. Caesar salad with croutons: croutons contain gluten, so Marcus cannot eat it (celiac); also traditional Caesar dressing contains garlic, so Priya cannot eat it (Jain, no root vegetables/alliums). Roasted potato wedges: potato is a root vegetable, so Priya cannot eat it (Jain). Two items are fine. Gluten-free salted caramel brownies: fine for everyone — Uncle Richard's sodium restriction was removed by his doctor, and these are already gluten-free for Marcus. Fresh fruit platter: fine for everyone.
required_elements: Honey-glazed ham is problematic: Priya is from a Jain household and cannot eat meat
Walnut-crusted chicken is problematic: contains walnuts which Aunt Helen is allergic to (tree nut allergy confirmed by allergist), and is also meat which Priya cannot eat
Caesar salad with croutons is problematic: croutons contain gluten which Marcus cannot eat (celiac disease)
Roasted potato wedges are problematic: potato is a root vegetable which Priya cannot eat (Jain dietary practice)
Gluten-free salted caramel brownies are fine for everyone currently attending — agent confirms they are acceptable
Fresh fruit platter is fine for everyone — agent confirms it is acceptable
Uncle Richard has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent does not flag sodium as a concern for any item
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item as problematic for Uncle Richard due to sodium (his low-sodium restriction was removed by his doctor)
Saying Aunt Helen only has a peanut allergy without mentioning tree nuts (her allergy was upgraded to include all tree nuts)
Saying Priya has a general allergy or medical condition (her dietary restriction is religious/cultural, from Jain practice)
Flagging the gluten-free salted caramel brownies as problematic for Uncle Richard due to salt or sodium
Over-generalizing Aunt Helen's tree nut allergy to all legumes or all seeds
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and constraint state changes across a memorial reception food planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Cousin Priya grew up in a traditional Jain household → Jain dietary laws → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including onion, garlic, potato (inferential chain, never explicitly listed as rules), (2) Uncle Richard's low-sodium diet is REMOVED mid-conversation when his doctor clears him — the agent must stop applying this constraint, (3) Nephew Marcus JOINS late with celiac disease (gluten-free requirement) — tests if agent remembers late additions, (4) Aunt Helen's allergy is UPGRADED from peanut-only to all tree nuts based on her daughter's correction and allergist confirmation. At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Priya=Jain (no meat, no root vegetables including garlic and potato), Helen=peanut and tree nut allergy (walnut is a tree nut), Marcus=celiac (no gluten, croutons are wheat-based), Richard=no restrictions (cleared by doctor). The gluten-free salted caramel brownies are a trap: they sound problematic for Richard (salted + rich dessert after heart surgery) but his restriction was explicitly removed. The Caesar salad tests multi-constraint awareness: croutons affect Marcus AND garlic in the dressing affects Priya.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
